review: 2:1–2:2 כָּל־דָּבָר הוּא הֶפְסֵד / וְכַזֶּבֶל — Philippians 3:8 (הֶפְסֵד … וְנֶחְשָׁב כְּזֶבֶל); the Arabic كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هُوَ خُسْرٌ وَنُفَايَةٌ is that verse, and נֶחְשָׁב is kept because the counting is the point.
3:1–3:2 יֶתֶר דַּעַת — 'the surpassing knowledge' (Phil 3:8, יֶתֶר דַּעַת); the Arabic فَضْلُ مَعْرِفَةِ is that phrase, and Hebrew uses the construct יֶתֶר for 'surpassing'.
4:2 אַתָּה צִדְקֵנוּ — Jer 23:6 (יְהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ); the Arabic أَنْتَ بِرُّنَا الْعَجِيب applies the title to Christ, as the New Testament does.

5:1–5:3 — the three phrases are Philippians 3:10 in order (the power of His resurrection, the fellowship of His sufferings, conformity to His death); Hebrew keeps all three with שֻׁתָּפוּת and הִדָּמוּת, the standard liturgical terms.
